module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Number of squares $\bmod n$

The number of squares modulo $n$.
This is the cardinality of the set $\{k^2 \bmod n \mid k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}\}$.

*References:*
- [A000224](https://oeis.org/A000224)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA224

/-- The number of squares modulo $n$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n = 0 then 1
  else
    Finset.card ((Finset.range n).image (fun k : ℕ => k ^ 2 % n))

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 2 := by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 2 := by decide

/--
$n^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{a(n)(a(n)-1)}$ if and only if $n$ is an odd prime.
- Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    (n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2) ↔ n ^ 2 ≡ 1 [MOD a n * (a n - 1)] := by
  sorry

end OeisA224

findings.description: The attribution in the docstring gives “Thomas Ordowski, Jun 08 2017,” but the cited OEIS entry dates this exact conjecture Apr 13 2025. This is a reference-date slip; the mathematical statement is faithful.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A000224, comment in revision 111: “Conjecture: n^2 == 1 (mod a(n)*(a(n)-1)) if and only if n is an odd prime. - Thomas Ordowski, Apr 13 2025.” Read through the official data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/0511d9a82701173fc7b4e49d4b9794132b657209/seq/A000/A000224.seq. The inspected April 12, 2025 revision does not yet contain the conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “Jun 08 2017” with “Apr 13 2025” in the conjecture's attribution.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly assumes n > 1, where the source leaves the requirement of a positive congruence modulus implicit. It also expresses “odd prime” as n.Prime ∧ n ≠ 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: OEIS starts at n=1, with a(1)=1, so the proposed modulus is zero there. For every n>1, the square-residue image contains the distinct residues 0 and 1, giving a(n)≥2 and a positive modulus. Thus, among positive indices, positivity of the modulus is equivalent to n>1. A prime is odd exactly when it is not 2. The scratch lemma formulation_equivalent proves the full ↔ between the Lean formulation and the source's image-count formulation over positive indices with positive modulus, without using the sorry-proved conjecture.

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A000/A000224.seq (official mirror of the cited https://oeis.org/A000224 entry)
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. No substantive mathematical defect was found. The definition agrees exactly with OEIS's Maple square-counting algorithm for n>0. Its a(0)=1 branch and a_0 test specify an extension outside OEIS's domain and do not affect the conjecture. Lean verified the first 72 published terms, checked the conjecture computationally for 2≤n≤200, and proved that natural subtraction and the modulus are nondegenerate throughout the theorem's domain. Experiments and equivalence proofs are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. OEIS still labels the statement a conjecture and records verification through 10^8, consistent with research open. The main OEIS page was Cloudflare-blocked; its full entry was read through the official OEIS data mirror.
